banner.comment: *** Key checkpoint at the top level: *** and its continuations.
banner.name: entity.name.section.banner.acl2-output

summary-label.comment: Only the label. What follows is prose or a form, and Rules: has its own rule.
summary-label.name: keyword.control.summary.acl2-output

goal-header.comment: A goal name alone on its line: Goal, Goal', Subgoal *1/2'', *1. Anchored to end-of-line, because `*1 (the initial Goal...) is pushed` is prose that opens the same way.
goal-header.name: entity.name.section.goal.acl2-output

rules-list.comment: `Rules: nil`, or a rune list running over several indented lines.

pe-form.comment: `pe` and friends print a form after a label column: ` L         4  (defun ...`.

term-block.comment: A term printed at column zero, continuing while its lines stay indented -- which is how ACL2 prints goals and induction schemes. Two guards on the opening line. `([` is excluded: it opens a checkpoint bracket whose line is prose. And the line must END in a close paren, because ACL2 wraps prose to about seventy columns and a sentence that happens to begin with a term (`(acl2-count x).  We observe that ...`) otherwise opens a block. ACL2's printer breaks after complete subterms, so a real term's first line almost always closes one; the cost is missing a term whose first line ends in a bare symbol, and under-highlighting is the right way to be wrong here.

island.comment: The real ACL2 grammar, but only ever inside a block whose extent is decided by indentation. `while` is re-tested at the start of every line and pops the block regardless of what is open inside it, so an unterminated string in a truncated term costs one block rather than the rest of the log. That containment is the whole design.
